newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST - POLISH 1996 CPI SEEN BELOW 18 PCT - C.BANK.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - POLISH 1996 CPI SEEN BELOW 18 PCT - C.BANK.

text.p: Polish inflation will not exceed 18 percent year-on-year in December this year after rising by 21.6 percent in 1995, the deputy president of the National Bank of Poland told Rzeczpospolita daily.
"Inflation at the end of this year, in comparison to December 1995, will definately not be higher than 18 percent," Witold Kozinski was quoted as saying.
The government's 1996 inflation target is 17 percent and consumer prices grew 11.3 percent in the January-July period.
Consumer prices rose year-on-year 20.4 percent in July.
Kozinski also said money supply would grow quicker than expected in 1996 because of the rapid rise in credit action.
He said broad money supply could grow by 28 billion zlotys this year, or by some 27 percent, instead of the planned 23 billion zlotys.
Credit to the non-financial sector increased by 20.6 percent in the first eight months of 1996, including a 56.6 percent rise in credit to households.
Broad money supply rose 16.7 percent in January-August.
